title: Goodwill Amounts and the Member Discount on Bench Labour
content:
# Service Training Note: Goodwill Amounts and the Member Discount on Bench Labour

## The rule the desk applies

An amount is taken off a priced line of a work order at the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service as goodwill where the chain itself fell short, and each service level carries its own allowance for how often that may be done. The allowance is 3 such amounts in the rolling twelve calendar months ending on the handling date, counted as the goodwill service recovery amounts already taken off for that customer in that window; where the allowance is exhausted the desk explains the allowance and does not take the amount off, and the customer's dissatisfaction alone is not a ground for passing that allowance.

A goodwill amount is taken off only when no amount has already been taken off that same priced line. Whether an amount has already been taken off is read from the entries standing against that priced line before the goodwill amount is taken off, whether the earlier amount was taken off as a goodwill service recovery, under a member benefit or under the workmanship guarantee.

Members of the loyalty programme receive the level's member discount on bench labour, and the member discount is applied to labour before any goodwill amount is considered. The member discount is the unit price of the labour multiplied by the number of units, taken at the level's member discount share, rounded to the nearest cent.

The member discount and a goodwill amount may both be taken off the same order, but never twice off the same priced line, and a rework carried out under the guarantee is recorded under the guarantee rather than as goodwill.

## Points of judgement

| The records show | A goodwill amount may be taken off that line |
|---|---|
| Nothing yet taken off that priced line, 2 goodwill recoveries in the last twelve months | yes |
| Nothing yet taken off that priced line, 3 goodwill recoveries in the last twelve months | no, the allowance is exhausted |
| A member benefit amount already taken off that same priced line | no |
| A goodwill amount already taken off a different priced line of the same order | yes, as to this line |

## A worked member discount on hypothetical inputs

At a level whose member discount is 10 percent, a labour line of 3 units priced at 140.00 USD each comes to 420.00 USD, and the member discount on it is 42.00 USD. Where the chain had also fallen short on that order, a goodwill amount could stand against another priced line of it, but not a second time against this one.
